newsitem.title: CANADA: Study documents loss of Montreal head offices.
newsitem.headline: Study documents loss of Montreal head offices.

text.p: More than 500 head offices have left Montreal for Toronto over the last 20 years, according to a study by Dun & Bradstreet released on Wednesday.
"In the last 20 years more than 506 head offices have left Montreal for Toronto, while only 122 have come the other way," the report said.
The study was commissioned by the Quebec Committee for Canada, a citizens' group that advocates Canadian unity.
"This business exodus is mainly due to the political uncertainty caused by Quebec's uncertain status within Canada," said Jean Briere, a member of the committee, in a statement.
He said the study does not take into account the transfer of corporations' departments and divisions from Montreal to Toronto.
The report examines the period dating back to the election of the first separatist Parti Quebecois government in 1976.
Of the 506 companies that left Montreal, more than 120 employed more than 100 people each, while only 20 companies of comparable size left Toronto for Montreal.
The ratio of departures from Montreal to arrivals of mid-sized companies was 5-to-1, while it was 8-to-1 for companies with less with 50 employees, the study said.
